claim: In the matching retail DLL, PlayerController_AI.TryToDoPriorityAct (0x06005009) is an instance method with one AIPriorityActEnum parameter named act returning Int32 and an exact 606-byte body. It switches on raw act with 41 explicit cases. Raw acts 0..5 and 6..7 index PriotityActToAIOpt[act], call SetAIAct_DownAtk(mapped value,180,1), store currentPriAct=act, then reach raw return 1. Raw acts 8..9 map the act, call PlObj.GetSkillData_Equip(mapped value,0), call GetDiveCorner_LR(TargetPlIdx,skill), return 0 when that result is -1, otherwise raw act 8 calls SetAIAct_RunUpDive_Stand and raw act 9 calls SetAIAct_RunUpDive_Down, then currentPriAct=act and return 1. Raw acts 10..13 map the act and load equipped SkillData; when PlObj.State is raw 6 they use PlObj.PostPos, otherwise call GetDiveCorner(TargetPlIdx,skill) and return 0 on -1; they then call SetAIAct_CornerDive(position,mapped value,0), store currentPriAct=act, and return 1. Raw acts 14..17 set padPush = PerformanceKeyTbl[PriotityActToAIOpt[act]-86], set currentPriAct=-1, and return raw 2 immediately. Raw acts 18..20 call SetAIAct_PriAct_RunAtk(mapped value,768); raw act 21 calls SetAIAct(17,768); raw acts 22..34 call SetAIAct_GoGrapple(mapped value,2,32); raw acts 35..40 call SetAIAct_GoBackGrapple(mapped value,32). Those paths store currentPriAct=act and return 1. The switch default also reaches raw return 1. FACT-0037 pins the direct call at ProcessPriorityAct IL+0x0180.
